title: Times tables as rows of dots
examples: How do I use dots to multiply?

explain.say: Imagine an egg box with three rows of four eggs. How many eggs? Look at the board. Dots in neat rows and columns are called an array. Arrays make times tables easy to see.

draw.text: Times tables as rows of dots

explain.say: Look at one row: four dots. One row of four is four. Can you tap each dot in the row?
Add another row. Two rows of four: four, eight. So two times four is eight. Count in fours, row by row. Can you guess how many three rows will be?
Three rows of four: four, eight, twelve! Three times four is twelve. Skip count the rows, and you never need to count every dot.

Now here is a trick. Turn the array on its side: four rows of three. Still twelve dots! So three times four and four times three give the same answer. Amazing! Challenge: find an array at home, like a muffin tray.

faq.a: An array is a picture of things in equal rows and columns, like eggs in a box. It shows multiplication.

faq.q: How do I use an array to multiply?
faq.a: Count how many are in one row, then skip count by that number for each row. Three rows of four: four, eight, twelve.
asks: How do I count an array?

faq.a: Turn the array around and the dots do not change. Three rows of four and four rows of three both have twelve dots.
asks: Does the order matter in times tables?

faq.q: Where can I find arrays in real life?
faq.a: Egg boxes, muffin trays, window panes, chocolate bars and cinema seats are all arrays.

faq.q: How can I make my own arrays?
faq.a: Use buttons, coins or stickers and put them in neat rows. A teacher or grown-up can give you a times question to build.
asks: How do I build an array?

facts: Multiplying two numbers in either order gives the same answer.

quiz.say: How many dots are in 2 rows of 5?
quiz.why: Five, ten: two rows of five make ten.

wrong.1: Seven is two add five. An array is two lots of five.

quiz.why: Turn the array around: four rows of three is still twelve.
